unit.why: A short anecdote (someone slaps R. Elimelech, who forgives him wholeheartedly) and a reported saying of his about the messiah, quoted from an earlier book and set inside a homiletic explanation of why the wicked persecute tzaddikim.
unit.boundary_note: Quoted from ס' בשביל אמונה; the next division begins a new quoted story from ס' ס"ה.

stories.summary_en: Someone strikes R. Elimelech of Lizhensk on the cheek and he forgives him so that no one will be punished on his account. The narrator's father-in-law heard him say that if two women would stop quarrelling over him, he would bring the messiah, and that he had already sweetened the decrees foretold for the end of days. A homily follows on why persecution by wicked people refines the tzaddik.
